title: Komodo Dragon Teeth Have Iron Edges. Nobody Noticed Until 2024

scenes.text: A Komodo dragon's teeth have orange edges. Nobody asked why.
It's the biggest lizard alive, up to ten feet long, and it brings down prey as large as water buffalo.
Its teeth are curved, serrated blades, like a meat-eating dinosaur's. But the enamel on them is thin. They ought to go blunt fast.
In 2024, a scientist going through skulls in museum collections kept seeing an orange line along every cutting edge. X-rays showed what it was. Iron.
A coat of iron on each tip and serration, keeping the blade sharp. It had never been reported in any meat-eating reptile.
Which raises a bigger question. T. rex had the same kind of teeth, and fossils can't tell us whether they were iron-edged too.

description:
Komodo dragons have a coating of iron on the cutting edges and tips of their teeth.
The orange, iron-rich layer was reported in Nature Ecology and Evolution in July 2024 by a team led by Aaron LeBlanc of King's College London, after examining Komodo dragon teeth from museums and zoos. It reinforces the thin enamel on the serrations and keeps them sharp. Other monitor lizards and crocodiles have some iron in their teeth, but far less concentrated. Whether carnivorous dinosaurs such as T. rex had the same thing is unknown, because fossilisation hides how much iron was there.
Do you think T. rex had iron teeth too?
